grh_4016458f9b786649b8e8.title: Mr Meeks
paragraphs: Eleanor Meeks loves her husband Gregory but is embarrassed by his contentment with gardening, seed catalogs and time with their son. She wants the president of the family manufacturing company to become more ambitious and important, so Christian helps draw Gregory back into civic and business responsibilities. The change soon produces a much more serious problem. A government tent contract calls for twelve-ounce canvas, but the Meeks company has delivered eight-ounce material while charging for the heavier grade. Suspicion falls on Gregory, especially because his forceful secretary Doris Handen is the sister of a politically connected man long suspected of graft. Christian uncovers a forged factory order and tricks Doris into admitting that the Handens manipulated the order and used Gregory's inattention as cover; John Hewitt overhears the confession so it cannot simply be denied. At home Eleanor then confronts a second apparent scandal, the rumor that Gregory has spent night after night at Doris's house. Gregory admits the visits, but the explanation is absurdly innocent: Eleanor had forbidden his beloved seed catalogs around their own home, so he went elsewhere to read them. The crisis clears Gregory of both fraud and infidelity and leaves Eleanor facing the comic truth that trying to remake a harmless, contented husband nearly created the very troubles she feared.

This [[show|dr-christian|Dr. Christian]] broadcast aired on March 21, 1939. It is listed as episode 48 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Jean Hersholt, Rosemary De Camp, Margaret Brayton, [[person|gale-gordon|Gale Gordon]], and [[person|gerald-mohr|Gerald Mohr]]. Other credited names include Art Gilmore as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 29 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.8830590ae040a6fd|Vaseline (World's Fair contest)]].

grh_4037641824bb27025be6.title: First Star Tonight
paragraphs: Television star Lisa Chadwick is already questioning the career and identity she built around fame when she is asked to help Marilyn Todd, a struggling young actress threatening to jump from a studio ledge. Marilyn initially sees Lisa as proof that stardom would solve everything, but Lisa admits that success left her empty enough to attempt suicide herself. Their conversation shifts from rescue to the question of whether either woman believes her life has value apart from Hollywood approval. Marilyn finally comes in from the ledge after realizing she wants to live, and Lisa recognizes that she needed the encounter too, admitting that she no longer knows whether the television persona she fought to protect is the life she wants.

[[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Cecily Tyson, Anne Burr, Anne Gibbon, Jack Carol, and Daws Butler. Other credited names include Fletcher Markle as director, Fletcher Markle as producer, and Pamela Russell as writer.
The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.9b0a0ccffce2f7d3|Sears, Roebuck and Company]].

grh_406ea595955d669a9de6.title: Horse Play
paragraphs: Harry creates an elaborate fake betting club in Paris to swindle wealthy American Harris into wagering on a supposedly fixed horse race. The staged telephones, cashiers and track information convince Harris to put up $28,000, but the scheme goes wrong when Harry's partner Janine mistakenly buys a win ticket instead of the intended safer bet and the horse runs second. Harry then stages Janine's shooting with blanks and fake blood, terrifying Harris into fleeing France because he believes he is implicated in murder. Before Harry can enjoy the money, real police raid the bogus club and seize almost everything. He escapes prison but is left with only a tiny fraction of the planned score.

The surviving recording runs about 27 minutes. Characters credited in this version include [[character|Harry Lime]].

grh_402ab6ca4b70514a7d86.title: Faith of Our Fighters-The Bid Was Four Hearts
paragraphs: A dramatization of the final voyage of the troop transport Dorchester follows Army chaplains George Fox, Alexander Goode, Clark Poling and John Washington as they minister to soldiers of different faiths aboard ship. When the Dorchester is torpedoed near Greenland, panic spreads as men struggle for lifeboats and life jackets. The four chaplains help others to safety and each gives his own life jacket to a soldier who has none. Witnesses later remember seeing the chaplains praying together on the slanting deck as the ship sinks beneath them.

The cast includes Martin Blaine, Harold Huber, James Monks, Carl Emory, and Lamont Johnson. Other credited names include Anton M. Leader as director, Timothy Mulvey as radio adaptor, and Jack Costello as host.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes.
This version dramatizes [[work|work.words.dce8c10fbd7a6740|Faith of Our Fighters-The Bid Was Four Hearts]]. Elwood C. Nantz is credited as author and Timothy Mulvey adapted it for radio.

grh_40db2c18852a4a0e083b.title: Rogue's Holiday
paragraphs: After a profitable swindle in New York, Harry sails for England and targets a wealthy woman he believes to be an aristocrat traveling with an extraordinarily valuable string of pearls. She eventually gives him the pearls as security for a $10,000 loan, and Harry leaves believing he has acquired a fortune. A London fence then tells him the pearls are imitations and the supposed noblewoman is Doris Jones, a confidence artist from Clapham. Harry's loss has one final twist: the $10,000 he gave her was counterfeit. When they meet again later, each recognizes the other's trick with no hard feelings.

This [[show|the-lives-of-harry-lime|The Lives of Harry Lime]] broadcast aired on September 21, 1951. It is listed as episode 8 in the archive. The cast includes [[person|orson-welles|Orson Welles]] and Anton Karas. Other credited names include Tig Roe as director and Harry Alan Towers as producer.

grh_400e4d2981cf06dbd30a.title: Sailor Framed for Murder

grh_40f62ede4dc1518ebbd7.title: Cherchez La Gem
paragraphs: Harry becomes involved in a hunt for about $75,000 in hidden jewels in Honolulu, with a rival named Brissie willing to use a gun to get them first. Harry survives the pursuit and gets the jewels into a car, only to learn that Moana wants no part of the fortune because it came from her late stepfather and could bring scandal on her family. At a cliff she deliberately lets the car roll into the Pacific with the jewels still inside. Harry manages to grab only a half bottle of Scotch from the back seat and is left with a kiss instead of the money.

grh_4006e06efa4845fa0671.title: A Little Game on Saturday Mornings
paragraphs: Two boys, Jeff and David, spend Saturday morning playing soldier under the command of their General, whom they also call Dad, as he reenacts heroic battlefield stories and dies gloriously in their game. The fantasy gradually breaks apart when attendants in white uniforms arrive to return the General to his chair at a veterans' home. The boys are revealed not as real children but as the family the permanently disabled veteran never had, imagined every Saturday as he relives a war that destroyed the life he might have lived.

grh_40844a6eddf8b8fcab80.title: Bachelor Mother
paragraphs: Department-store clerk Polly Parish is mistakenly believed to be the mother of an abandoned baby and cannot convince her employer, David Merlin, that the child is not hers. David first forces her to care for the infant, then becomes increasingly involved with both Polly and the baby while his father enthusiastically assumes he has become a grandfather. After escalating misunderstandings over the child's parentage, David realizes he loves Polly and proposes, happily accepting the ready-made family he still believes is hers.
